about: Known KTM-family CAN broadcast IDs, for labelling the bus sniffer. Every layout here comes from OTHER bikes. Nobody has published a capture from a 2013-16 (Gen 1) Duke, so treat each row as a hint to test on your bike, not a fact. Edit this file, then run tools/gen_can_ids.py.

status.confirmed: checked against the dash or the bike's behaviour, by the project's owner or against a labelled capture log
status.capture: found in a real capture, not cross-checked (unit or meaning may be a guess)
status.reported: stated in a forum post, no capture to check
status.candidate: educated guess from the byte pattern

ktmcan.title: blalor/ktm-can (690 Enduro R; decoding credited to Dan Plastina's 1290 Super Duke thread, 2017)

ktmcomp.title: ChickenPoptart/KTMComputer, docs/can-signals.md (690 Enduro R, with ride captures)

ktm1390.title: sruon/ktm-1390-can (1390 Super Duke R Evo: README plus 17 candump logs, which I checked the README against)

racechrono.title: RaceChrono forum: KTM 890 Duke R CAN-bus thread (RaceChrono PIDs are decimal: 299 = 0x12B, 303 = 0x12F)

advrider.title: ADVrider: Results from hacking the KTM SuperDuke 1290 CAN bus (quoted by ktm-can)

ids.name: Engine: rpm, throttle, switches
ids.try: Key on, then rev the engine or twist the grip. Flip the kill switch. Press start.

fields.name: Throttle grip (commanded)
fields.note: raw 0 = closed, 253-255 = fully open. 1390 Evo: 0 at idle, 24-44 on the blips in the start-up log

fields.name: Kill switch
fields.note: the same bit the 690 uses for the kill switch is the start button here. 1390 Evo: 08 with the switch on RUN, 00 on STOP

fields.name: Start button
fields.note: 1390 Evo: D3 = 18 while cranking

fields.name: Ride mode
fields.note: names assumed from the menu order

fields.text: alive counter, steps by 0x20 (30, 50, 70, 90, B0, D0)

ids.name: Throttle grip sensors
ids.try: Twist the grip with the key on. Two bytes should rise together.
ids.note: D1 and D3 rise with the grip: probably the two redundant ride-by-wire sensors. 1390 Evo: D5 tracked engine speed closely in the start-up log (correlation 0.8), so the layout may differ there.

fields.text: rolling counter

ids.name: Throttle closed switch
ids.try: Key on: twist the grip off its stop and let go.
ids.note: 690: reads 7F FF ... until the ECU wakes, then D2 toggles 02/03 with the engine running. 1390 Evo: D0-D1 stay 13 88 and D2 steps 01, 02, 03 through a start-up, so there it is a state, not a throttle switch (the repo README says gear and clutch live here, but its clutch log shows them in 129).

ids.name: Gear and clutch
ids.try: Key on, engine off: roll the bike and change gear. Pull the clutch lever.
ids.note: 701 Enduro: the 701display firmware watches D0 bit 3 going LOW to spot the off-road ABS button being held while stopped. 1390 Evo: the clutch bit toggled in its lever-pull log; gear stayed 0 (neutral) in every log, so gear is unchecked there.

fields.text: alive counter, steps by 0x20 (20, 40, 60, 80, A0, C0)

ids.name: Ride mode, traction and ABS states
ids.try: Bike stopped: change ride mode, press the TC button, switch ABS mode.
ids.note: The bit positions differ between models, so try each variant against what you change.

fields.name: Traction control
fields.note: D1 = 28 on, 18 off. Offroad ride mode also turns it off.

fields.name: ABS mode
fields.note: names not known

fields.name: Slip adjuster (MTC) level
fields.note: 1C = 7, 20 = 8, 24 = 9 while stepping the slip adjuster 7, 8, 9, 8, 7

fields.text: 1390 Evo: D2 high nibble is 7 in Performance and 1 in Rain (anti-wheelie level, per the repo). D4 moved with the ride mode (60, 44, 04, 24 seen).

ids.name: ABS wheel speeds and lean
ids.try: Bike on a stand, key on: spin the front wheel by hand, then the rear. Lean the bike on the stand for tilt and lean.
ids.note: Not sent at all on the 390 Adventure (Gen 2) or the 1390 Evo (no 12B in any of its 17 logs); a RaceChrono commenter says 0x12B does not carry wheel speed on the 890 R. Scale: 701 Enduro fitted 17.77 counts per km/h against its OBD speed; the 690 speedometer gave about 17.0. Lean: 0 is upright, 1 and up lean right, FFF and down lean left (1290 thread). A 790 forum post (no ID given) says speed is (D0*256+D1)/16, unverified. One RaceChrono commenter (hedged with 'if I remember correctly') put front and rear wheel speed at PID 299 (= 0x12B) as bit ranges, calling them ABS pulse frequencies, which fits the layout here; another says 299 carries no wheel speed on the 890 R.

fields.name: Rear wheel speed
fields.note: agrees with the front within about 3%

fields.name: Tilt (raw)
fields.note: 12-bit signed, not validated

fields.name: Lean angle (raw)
fields.note: 12-bit signed; degrees per count not published

fields.text: all zero when stopped; two 12-bit values follow wheel speed (slower, different scale)

ids.name: Rear wheel speed (390 Adventure)
ids.try: Bike on a stand: spin the rear wheel by hand. Compare with the dash on a ride.
ids.note: Also sent on the 1390 Evo (about every 10 ms); with the wheels still only the counter in D7 changed.

fields.name: Rear wheel speed
fields.note: a per-pulse count; the unit (0.1 km/h per count) is a guess, calibrate against the dash

ids.name: Smoothed speed (390 Adventure)
ids.note: 690: D0 is a status flag (00/40) and D7 a counter. Also sent on the 1390 Evo; with the bike still D6 and D7 changed there.

fields.name: Speed, smoothed
fields.note: about 0.7 x the 12D value, fades out after the wheel stops

ids.name: Lean angle (rear brake?)
ids.try: Tilt the bike on its stand. Then press only the rear pedal. See which one moves D0-D1.
ids.note: Evidence for lean: on the 1390 Evo D0-D1 sat at F83x (-125 counts) with the bike upright on its stand and ignored the rear pedal, and a RaceChrono commenter guesses lean/tilt is at PID 303 (= 0x12F) on the 890 R, which has the newer Super Duke ABS (a guess, no capture). The 390 Adventure project claims both uses for D0-D1 and has not settled it. D1 bit 0x20 also flips in bursts there (a status bit, not identified).

fields.name: Lean angle (raw)
fields.note: tilted by hand on the stand: negative left, positive right. 1390 Evo upright on its stand: -125, jittering by 1-2 counts

fields.name: Rear brake (raw)
fields.note: rests near 304, rises 50-90 with the pedal (390 Adventure). The 1390 Evo's D0-D1 did not move with the pedal

ids.name: Handlebar buttons (1390 Evo)
ids.try: With the key on, use the turn-signal switch, the cancel button and the high-beam flash and watch which bit pulses.
ids.note: Each button sets its own bit while held, and D2 rests at 03. The four below were checked against the repo's turn-signal and high-beam logs. The repo README counts bits from the left (its B0 is 0x80); everything here uses bit 0 = 0x01. Newer switchgear: whether a Gen 1 sends this is unknown.

fields.text: Other bits, from the repo README only (not checked one by one): D0 bit 1 = C1, bit 0 = C2; D1 bit 7 = cruise, bit 4 = +/resume, bit 3 = -/set, bit 1 = horn; D2 bit 7 right, 6 left, 5 up, 4 down, 3 centre of the d-pad. D2 bit 2 also pulses in the button log.

ids.name: Motion sensor (IMU)?
ids.try: Lean the bike on the stand and watch which of 174, 178 and 17C swings.
ids.note: Also on the 1390 Evo, where almost every byte jitters even with the bike upright on its stand.

fields.text: two 16-bit values centred near 0x8000 (one offset by gravity); counter in D6 low nibble; checksum in D7
D0 and D4 jitter at rest; D6 low nibble counts 0-F; D7 looks like a checksum. Large erratic jumps = raw sensor data, not a clean speed.
D4 jitters at rest; D6 low nibble counts 0-F; D7 looks like a checksum.

ids.name: Motion sensor (IMU)?
ids.try: Lean the bike on the stand: D0-D1 should swing.

fields.name: Lean candidate
fields.note: swings most when the bike leans

fields.text: counter in D6 low nibble; checksum in D7

ids.name: Motion sensor (IMU)?
ids.try: Lean the bike on the stand: D4-D5 should swing.

fields.name: Lean candidate
fields.note: swings most when the bike leans

fields.text: counter in D6 low nibble; checksum in D7

ids.name: Brake pressure and brake light
ids.try: Key on: squeeze the front lever, then press the rear pedal.
ids.note: 690: D2-D7 stay 0, so there is no brake-light bit there.

fields.name: Front brake pressure (raw)
fields.note: 390 Adventure: rest noise up to about 48, firm stop 15,000-20,000. 1390 Evo: 0 at rest, about 8,500 at the peak of a hard squeeze on the stand

fields.name: Front brake lever switch
fields.note: D3 = 02 at rest, 0A with the lever

fields.name: Rear brake pedal switch
fields.note: D3 = 06 with the pedal. Rear pedal pressure did not show in D0-D1 (peak 32)

fields.text: 390 Adventure: D3 goes 02 to 0E when the brake light is on (both bits at once), unlike the 1390 Evo where each switch has its own bit
always 0F... on the 690; maybe the off-road ABS dongle, untested with it unplugged
D0-D3 are either 71 7A 4C 54 or FF FF FF FF (looks like four sensor values that read FF when invalid); D4-D5 stay 7D 7D. Meaning not known.
D0 reads 28 at rest and swings while the engine cranks (down to 0B, then back up); D1 is 80, sometimes C0; D7 is a counter. Meaning not known.
D0, D3 and D6 follow engine speed loosely (correlation about 0.7 in the start-up log); D1, D4 and D7 vary too. Meaning not known.

ids.name: Buttons and ABS mode
ids.try: Press the TC button and the map button. Change ABS mode with the bike stopped.
ids.note: 390 Adventure: D2 sits at 0x80 at rest, so the 690's TC-button bit may not apply. 1390 Evo: the top bits of D2 step through 20, 40, 60 ... between logs (a slow counter), and D4 changed (1B, 13, 0B, 03) in the logs where the ride mode was switched.

fields.name: ABS mode
fields.note: names assumed

ids.name: Start-up exchange (1390 Evo)
ids.note: Only 12 frames in the whole set, right after key-on: 4E8 = 55 01 ..., 55 02 ..., 55 03 ... with random-looking bytes, 4E9 = 5A 01 01, 5A 02 01, 5A 03 01. Looks like a key or security exchange, so there is nothing to decode.

fields.name: Orange warning light
fields.note: D4 = 01 in the log taken with the kill switch off, all zero in every other log; the repo README names it as the dashboard's orange light

ids.name: Slow status: coolant, gear, stand, fuel
ids.try: Key on: raise and lower the side stand. Warm the engine and compare coolant with the dash.
ids.note: The 690 and 390 Adventure put coolant and the side stand one byte apart, so the variants disagree. Whichever gives a believable number is the one for your bike. The 1390 Evo agrees with the 390 Adventure for coolant.

fields.name: Coolant
fields.note: 96.2 after a ride (390 Adventure). 1390 Evo: 95.8 in a warm-engine log, 15.4 on a cold key-on, climbing through a start-up; check against the dash

fields.name: Fuel flow (raw per second)
fields.note: 0 off, about 27 just after start, 19-22 idling; litres per hour not calibrated

fields.text: 1390 Evo: D3 reads 10 before the engine starts and 00 once it is running (meaning not known). D1 follows engine speed loosely but is not a clean copy.

ids.name: Quickshifter and timers
ids.note: 690: always 02 80. 390 Adventure: a byte counts seconds since start (D4 or D6 in the two captures), so it is a timer, not a sensor.

fields.text: seconds-since-start style counter

ids.name: Lights and status flags
ids.try: Switch the indicators, the hazards and the high beam on and off with the key on.

fields.text: 690: D0 flips between 00 and 10; D7 is a counter

fields.name: Left indicator lit
fields.note: toggles about every 0.4 s while flashing; both lit = hazards

ids.name: Static with engine off (390 Adventure)
ids.note: 1390 Evo: also static, 00 00 00 00 00 04 C0 00 in every log.

fields.text: static with the engine off; capture again riding
D0 and D7 vary (D7 looks like a counter); the other bytes stay put. Meaning not known.

ids.name: Slow static: trip or service data?

fields.text: 1 Hz, static: odometer, trip or service-interval candidate

fields.name: Odometer
fields.note: 21430 = 2,143 km on the dash (390 Adventure). 1390 Evo: 00 17 16 = 591.0 km in sixteen logs and 00 17 83 = 601.9 km in a later one, so it counts up as the bike is ridden

fields.text: 690: D1 and D2 change once after the ECU wakes. 390 Adventure: static with the engine off. 1390 Evo: D3-D6 sit at 62 44 92 80 and D7 is a counter.

ids.name: Suspension mode (semi-active)
ids.try: On a bike with electronic suspension, change the suspension profile and watch D0.
ids.note: Only bikes with electronic (semi-active) suspension: not a Gen 1 Duke.

fields.name: Suspension profile
fields.note: 99 (Track), AA (Pro) and 00 (Automatic) were seen while switching profiles; the other values are from the repo README

fields.text: preload: 58 = auto standard in every log (the README also lists 60 auto low, 68 auto high, 50 = 100%, D8 = 95%, 48 = 90%, 08 = 10%, 90 = 5%, 00 = 0%)
D0-D5 change a little (six different frames in the whole set). Meaning not known.
random-looking bytes with only two different frames in the whole set; probably a checksum or security value
capture again riding

ids.name: Multi-frame transport (dash?)
ids.note: D0 = 0F or 30 looks like multi-frame framing: probably the dash or a diagnostic transport, not live sensor data.

ids.name: OBD-II request to all modules
ids.note: Only appears while something is asking (a scan tool, or this unit's own requests).

ids.name: Engine ECU: request
ids.note: Confirmed on a 2015 390 Duke: the ECU listens on 7E0 and answers on 7E8.

ids.name: Engine ECU: reply
ids.note: Only appears in answer to a request. Confirmed on a 2015 390 Duke.

ids.name: Other module: request
ids.note: Physical request to another module (ABS, dash), seen while a scanner or Find modules is running.

ids.name: Other module: reply
ids.note: A module answering a request. Find modules lists who answered.
